title: Switching from Albert to Boehm system clarinet
summary: He bought a Boehm clarinet for his son, who lost interest, so Thomas taught himself the fingering and now can't play the Albert.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, that's it. That's the place. Well, I bought this clarinet for my son. So, he got to learn a little bit of horn at these. Learned pretty good, you know. And so he went to California with the horn. And then he came back again. And so, I noticed he wasn't bothering with it. I said, well, George, you know, you're not going to play the clarinet? He said, Dad, I don't care to play the horn. I said, well, no. I said, no. I said, well, I can't let it lay here and go to waste. So, I used to take that horn and my albert system to H and J on the job. I tried to play a number with the BAM system and I couldn't. I put it down and pick up the albert. So, finally, I got to learn the BAM system little by little. And now, I can't play the albert no more.
Oh, yeah, you got to work in the albert now.
Got to work in the albert.
Anybody else show you how the fingering was different on it? Or you worked it out yourself?

I worked it out myself, yeah. Worked it out yourself. Yeah, just felt my way myself because there wasn't no clarinet player. No, only anybody plays. No, and so, I just worked it out myself. Just kept feeling my way and finally got the BAM system to work in. Now, since that, I tried to play albert. And so, I got a different fingering, you know.
